title: header_typed.rs: parse_header_typed feeds already-decoded String back as bytes
description: mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs: parse_header_typed() takes a header value that has already been decoded from raw bytes (possibly with encoded-word unfolding by mail-parser), converts it to a String, then re-encodes it as bytes via .as_bytes() to feed back into MessageStream::new(&buf) for mail-parser's typed parsers (parse_address(), parse_date(), etc.). This round-trip (decoded → String → &[u8] → parse again) is necessary because mail-parser's typed APIs take byte slices, but it is non-obvious. The crlf_terminated() call adds another re-encode pass to ensure the mail-parser stream terminates correctly. A comment explaining why the round-trip is unavoidable (mail-parser typed API requires raw bytes, there is no 'parse from already-decoded string' path) would prevent a future reader from 'simplifying' the code by removing one of the encode steps.
